title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Sixth edition, Volume 20, SUI-ZYM - EB.11
text:
ULIETEA, one of the Society islands in the South
see. This island is about a llegoso in circuit. Its
productions are plantains, cocoon nuts, yams, hogs, and
fowl; the two latter of which are scarce. The soil on
the top of one of the hills was found to be a kind of
time marks; on the sides were found some scattered
flints, and a few small pieces of a cavernous or spongy
stone lava, of a wishlic colony, which seemed to contain
some remains of iron, so that it may possibly be here
lodged in the mountains in a great quantity. Nothing
was seen on this Island to distinguish either its inhibi-
tants, or their manners, from the other neighboring
slands. The first Europens who landed on this shore
were Mr (now Sir Joseph) Banks and Dr Sander;
they were received by the native time and courrous
manner, reports concerning them having been their bar-
bingers from Otahteite. Everybody seemed to fear and
respect them, placing in them at the near time the st-
most confidence: behavior as if conscious than their
visitors possessed the power of doing them mischief with
out a disposition to make use of it.
